title: Split a Windows path
description:
Write `splitPath(path)`, which splits a Windows file path into its folder, its file name without the extension, and its extension, the way a game might when deciding where to put a backup or which loader to use.

- The folder is everything before the last `\` or `/` (either separator may appear), without that separator. If there is no separator, the folder is empty.
- The extension is everything from the last `.` in the file-name part onwards, including the dot. A dot at the very start of the file name (as in `.gitignore`) does not start an extension. No dot means no extension.
- The stem is the file-name part without the extension.

```
C:\Games\Save\slot1.sav     ->  "C:\Games\Save", "slot1", ".sav"
levels/forest.v2.lvl        ->  "levels", "forest.v2", ".lvl"
README                      ->  "", "README", ""
C:\Users\.config            ->  "C:\Users", ".config", ""
```
hints: `find_last_of("\\/")` finds the last character that is either separator. Everything after it is the file name.
Look for the last dot only in the file name, not in the whole path, so a dot in a folder name is ignored. A dot at position 0 of the name does not count.
